subject: Re: Performance SLOs & context window - follow up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <ajohnson@finco.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finco.com>, Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLOs & context window - follow up

Hi Alex + Priya,

Thanks for a productive call this morning — appreciate you walking us through FinCo's requirements. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same frame:

- Primary use case: document summarization + customer chat for support transcripts (mix of short and long sessions).
- Expected peak throughput: ~50 req/s for the summarization endpoint, with spikes to 80 req/s during end-of-quarter reporting.
- Typical input context sizes: 8k tokens for summaries; occasional 32k context for full transcript ingestion (about 5-10% of requests).
- Response sizes: mostly 200-600 tokens; some policy/incident reports up to 2k tokens.
- Latency SLO target: p95 end-to-end <= 800ms for 200-600 token responses; for larger 2k outputs we understand the SLO may be relaxed (target p95 <= 2s for those cases).
- Concurrency target: support 100 concurrent open chat sessions with streaming responses enabled (low-latency first-byte for UX).

Action items / next steps:
1) Ethan to propose an initial config (model variant + quantization + batching) and an estimate of required Dedicated capacity to hit the SLOs.
2) FinCo (Alex) to share example transcripts (anonymized) and single-request size distribution so we can run tokenized latency tests.
3) Marissa to send a draft mutual action plan and proposed commercial outline.

Attachments: draft MAP + placeholder for test results. We'll run a tokenized latency sweep once we get the sample traffic.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary.

Couple clarifications:
- For the 32k context requests, these will be bulk ingestion jobs (not interactive) but we still want to ensure they don't starve interactive chat traffic.
- Streaming: important that the first token arrives in <150ms after the model starts generating, otherwise our frontend shows a bad UX. We can't tolerate >300ms first-byte consistently.
- Can Redwood support token-level streaming for partial outputs (we'd like to stream as the model generates)?

I'll upload 50 anonymized transcripts to the shared Drive by EOD tomorrow.

Alex
Head of Platform, FinCo
From: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <ajohnson@finco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finco.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & context window - follow up

Alex — thanks, that's super helpful. Quick notes on feasibility and the tradeoffs we discussed on the call:

- Streaming: Yes, Redwood supports token-level streaming. Our streaming latency depends on model size, quantization, and batching. For a mid-sized open model (e.g., Llama2-13B-class optimized), we can typically get first-token TTL (time-to-first-token) ~80-120ms for short-context requests (<=8k) when under steady-state load with modest batching.

- Context window impact: moving from 8k -> 32k increases memory footprint and KV cache overhead. For 32k context, model execution time for the forward pass can increase by ~2.5-4x depending on attention implementation and sequence lengths of the response. That translates to longer per-request latency and lower throughput.

- Concurrency/throughput: to meet p95 <=800ms for 200-600 token outputs at 50 req/s, preliminary estimate is 4-6 Dedicated GPUs (A10s equivalent) with optimized kernels and medium batching (batch size 4-8). If you need strict p95 <=400ms at that throughput, we recommend 8+ GPUs or a smaller model variant.

- Large outputs (2k tokens): these are bandwidth-bound — streaming helps, but total time will still be multiple seconds. We can prioritize interactive traffic by routing long-batch ingestions to a separate pool (burst / background) to avoid interference.

I'll run a targeted latency sweep once you upload the transcripts — will share CSV results and config used.

Ethan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- model variants: optimized-13B / optimized-7B / low-latency-3B (quantized)

Target for lab tests: ETA by 2027-06-04 COB so Alex has something before their internal architecture review.

Received MAP — looks good at a glance. A couple of asks prior to our architecture review:
1) Can you include a short note in the MAP about routing policy to protect interactive traffic (e.g., separate pools + priority queueing)?
2) If possible, a short summary of how Redwood's KV cache/prefix cache will reduce token compute for repeated transcripts (we have many common headers and boilerplate in transcripts).

We expect to sign a pilot agreement if the lab tests align with the SLOs. Thanks for the quick work.

Alex
